newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AmEx in joint card talks with Australia banks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AmEx in joint card talks with Australia banks.

text.p: American Express Co's Australasian and South Pacific unit said on Monday it was in talks with Australia's major banks to form a strategic partnership with one of them, possibly to issue a joint co-branded card.

"We have said to all the banks, bar none, there may be markets that you're currently not accessing with your range of cards as they exist today," American Express' senior vice president for Australia, New Zealand/South Pacific, John Schaap, told Reuters after an address to the Institute of Chartered Accountants. "We're prepared to open our network if you believe we can strategically together develop some markets," he said.
American Express announced last month the formation of a strategic partership with Qantas Airways Ltd and said they would launch a co-branded card from February 1997.
"We're positioning ourselves as someone that's got a network that is prepared to share them if the strategic partnership works from both points of view."
Schaap said that in some countries American Express would stop and had stopped to issue cards itself, instead allowing another institution like a bank to manage the card.
But he said he did not think American Express would take this route in Australia.
"We've got a pretty good base here and it's a healthy base and it will continue to grow," he said.
Schaap said he could not speculate on how long such negotiations would take or with whom American Express was negotiating.
The co-branded corporate debt card to be launched with Qantas is the first such co-branded corporate card American Express has launched.
It is yet to launch a full co-branded card with a bank anywhere in the world, although it has launched co-branded personal cards with Delta, Sheraton and Peugeot.
Schaap said American Express' recent decision to launch co-branded cards was a fundamental shift of its strategy which had been based on keeping American Express' brand undiluted.
"The agonising that went on was quite profound," he said, adding however that the company's experience and customer surveys had found the brand had not been diluted.
Meanwhile Schaap said American Express' recently launched government purchases card had been a moderate success.
Federal government employees use the card as a corporate debit card and the government is sent statements detailing the purchases.
He said the card's launch had coincided with severe cutbacks in government spending and there had been some reluctance to use such a card given perceptions of abuse with previous cards.
"I still think there could be a bit more volume going through there."
